title: Choose the visual world for SakanHub
question: The roll assigned The Licence Plaque. Keep it, take my pick, or re-roll.

options.label: The Licence Plaque
options.lineage: The bilingual municipal licence plate fixed beside every licensed Saudi building: enamel plate, four screws, licence number, activity, capacity, QR
options.thesis: The request IS a plaque: the HR manager fills in city, workers and start date on a licence-style plate, and gets beds back. Every section is a plate screwed to a clay plaster wall.
materials: white enamel plates, four screw dots, rounded corners
bilingual field rows (Arabic right, English left), stamped reference numbers
options.viewport: A clay wall fills the screen. One large white plaque, screwed at four corners, carries the hook «سكن عمّالك… بطلب واحد» and three working fields — City · Workers · Start date — plus the Request beds action, set like the capacity rows of a real licence plate. The logo sits top-right as the building's name sign.
options.risk: Can tip into bureaucratic or 'government form' if the plates get dense; Nunito's rounded type and the warm clay wall have to keep it human.

raised.raise: Decisive beat: full-strength clay is reserved for one element per viewport, the primary action; everything else stays plate-white and ink.
Staged arrival: the scroll steps closer, city → building → room → bed, each plate tighter in scale than the last.
Total palette commitment: stock photos are duotoned into clay and ink, so no foreign colour enters the wall.

options.label: The Key Board
options.lineage: The pigeonhole key cabinet and bed-allocation board in every Saudi labour-camp office
options.thesis: Availability made physical: a grid of rooms and beds, keys hanging where a bed is free; requesting beds lifts keys off hooks.
options.viewport: A wide key board fills the screen; choosing city and headcount lifts that many keys and drops them into a request tray with the Request beds action.
options.risk: Implies live availability data we don't have yet; must be clearly illustrative until real inventory exists. It's also a more familiar 'grid of items' layout.

options.label: Teletext Service
options.case: Fuses poorly: retro broadcast novelty undercuts B2B trust; the cell grid fights bilingual RTL text.
options.kept: Addressable plates: every plaque carries a short reference code (RUH-01), and a request returns one.

options.label: Deco Cinema Lobby
options.case: Fuses poorly: premiere glamour has nothing to do with worker housing.
options.kept: Staged arrival thresholds (raised into the plaque direction).

options.label: Manga Screentone Page
options.case: Fuses poorly: an HR buyer doesn't identify with it; RTL panels are tempting but off-brand.
options.kept: Decisive beat: solid colour reserved for one element (raised).

options.label: Indoor Weather Sun
options.case: Fuses poorly: atmospheric art piece, no product clarity.
options.kept: Total palette commitment: duotone every photo (raised).

options.label: Cracktro Scroller Queue
options.case: Fuses poorly: a night-time hacker aesthetic for a daytime ops buyer.
options.kept: Rank is depth: hierarchy by scale and stillness, not by boxes.

options.label: Pickling Brine Calendar
options.case: Fuses poorly: food craft, no link to housing.
options.kept: Label banding: every listing plate banded with the same fields (city · licensing track · capacity).

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What worker-housing and proptech sites ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Photo of a compound, headline and request form, then a row of service cards.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from Mnzil and every AI-generated site, which is exactly what you said would feel wrong.
